_comment: What we have actually run, not what we recommend. Models age in weeks and this file is
fetched at runtime for that reason: a name compiled into the installer would still be
advertised long after it stopped being a sensible choice, and the installer does not
update itself.
Rules for adding a line here:
- only models someone on the project has actually run the instruction suite against
- 'note' says what was observed, in one sentence, with no superlative
- never a ranking: the suite is a heuristic on free text and the machine matters as much
as the model. The person testing decides; this only tells them where to start.
- NEVER pick or rank by language. Sorting by 'good at Japanese' would break the rule the
whole project is built on: every part of it stays language-agnostic.
NOTHING IS WITHHELD FOR SCORING BADLY. Every model here can be downloaded, with its figures
and what it missed written next to it. Offering only the spotless ones sounded prudent until
the measurements arrived: it left the smallest cards with no choice at all, on the grounds
that we knew better than the person who owns the machine. A model that misses one rare shape
may be the right trade for someone with 4 GB; that is their call, and it needs the figures.
WHAT MISSING A MARKER REALLY COSTS. Not silent corruption — the mod validates the markers
itself, retries up to three times, repairs a trailing line break, and if the model still
fails it leaves the line untranslated rather than caching a mangled one. The cost is up to
three times the calls, taken from the game's own GPU time, and text left in its original
language when a model keeps missing. Visible, not hidden.
'pull' IS PINNED TO A VERSION, NEVER 'latest'. A moving tag makes every figure below a lie
the day it moves, and the reader has no way of knowing which day that was.
⚠ 'match' is NOT the same thing and must not be pinned as tightly: it recognises what someone
already has, as a substring, longest match winning. Pinning it to an exact tag silently robs
everyone running ':latest' of their note. Hence the family entries below — they carry no
figures precisely because a moving tag has none to carry.
'measured' is the tester's own reading, as figures rather than prose, so a screen can sort
and compare them instead of stacking paragraphs. 'kept' counts draws of ONE line that came
back with every placeholder intact — a test of constancy. 'suite' counts instructions
followed across fifteen different cases — a test of breadth. Both are needed: a model can
pass one and fail the other.
⚠ EVERY FIGURE HERE WAS MEASURED TRANSLATING INTO ONE LANGUAGE — see 'measured_in'. A model
can hold its markers in one language and lose them in another: the text is tokenised
differently, comes back at a different length, and may not run in the same direction. Nothing
here transfers automatically to another target. The tester runs in the reader's own language,
which is the real answer: this file says where to start, the button says what happens.
⚠ THE SUITE WAS REBUILT ON 2026-08-10 and these figures are not comparable with earlier ones.
It had been sending marker rules the mod only sends when that marker is present, which made
several cases easier than reality, and its hardest line was 45 characters against a real
median of 73 and a ninth decile of 220. Every model here was re-run twice, idle machine, and
the two passes agreed case for case.
'min_vram_gb' is the card size below which the model runs on the processor instead, which
means minutes per line rather than seconds. It filters the offer; it never hides the list.
⚠ It is NOT the download size, and the two differ wildly in BOTH directions: gemma4:e2b-it-qat
downloads 4.3 GB and holds 1.7, qwen3:8b downloads 5.2 GB and takes 9.3. Every figure is a
measurement plus a gigabyte of headroom, rounded up to a card size that exists.
'languages' is the PUBLISHER'S claim, never our measurement — we have verified none of them.
Two numbers when they give two: a model tuned for 35 languages that merely saw 140 in
training is not the same promise, and the difference matters to whoever falls in the gap.
⚠ It stays a COUNT. Recording WHICH languages, and filtering the offer by what somebody is
translating into, is the one thing this project does nowhere.

models.note: What the mod is developed against, and one of only two here that also follows the experimental source-language rule. In a long text it wrote one tag marker as [!t1] instead of [!t*1] — the mod catches that and asks again.
Missed nothing across the whole suite, and follows the experimental source-language rule — the only model here to do both. Wants a card with room, and gives nothing up for it.
Missed nothing across the whole suite, but held 9.3 GB — nearly twice its download, and beyond most gaming cards. Check the memory figure before choosing it over something smaller.

The reference model's small sibling, in less than two thirds of the memory. It stretched a colour over a whole sentence instead of the one word it wrapped — worth knowing if your game colours words inside its lines.

The smallest footprint anything here has managed, and it gives up remarkably little for it: one case, a run of six numbered markers, where it answered with the word alone. Worth trying on a card nobody would call suitable.
The previous generation's small build, with the lightest download of the lot. Lost a blank line inside a text, and dropped a run of six numbered markers.

Swallowed a line break, gluing two sentences together, and cut a long text short — the end of it, with two markers, simply did not come back. Its lighter sibling e2b-it-qat did better in half the memory.
Built for translation and it shows in the prose, but it is the markers it struggles with: a blank line lost, a trailing line break swallowed, a colour left open, a run of numbers dropped.

Translates a long passage beautifully and then hands it back without its markers — the colour tags are simply gone. It also missed a placeholder on one draw in four of the same line, where its 4B sibling held all four.
Several sizes were run and each has its own line here. If this reads 'latest', the tag moves between versions, so no figure of ours applies to it — check which size it resolves to today.
Several builds were run and each has its own line here. If this reads 'latest', the tag moves between versions, so no figure of ours applies to it — check which build it resolves to today.

A whole family rather than one model, so no size or figure is given here. Gemma has no separate system turn — it is merged into the conversation, which makes it more sensitive to how instructions are phrased.

Reasons before answering, so every line costs noticeably more time. Not offered for download either: the smaller build is a 14 GB download and the other 65 GB, both beyond the cards this tool is aimed at.
